notes: Fix: the catalogue's arduino-mkr1000 card has only USB, VIN, VCC, GND and BAT, so it has no pin 2. I changed mkr1 to arduino-mkr1000-wifi, which has D2 and GND. It is catalogued as the MKR WiFi 1010, but it has the same MKR form factor and the same pin 2 and GND positions as the MKR 1000 in the tutorial's image. Both are 3.3 V logic. With 3.3 V, a 2 V LED and 220 ohm, the LED draws about 6 mA, within that card's 7 mA per-pin limit.

Circuit: D2 -> green wire -> breadboard column 3 -> 220 ohm resistor -> column 6 -> LED anode. The LED cathode is in column 8 -> black wire -> GND. The resistor is on the anode side, as in the schematic.
The image labels the breadboard rows j-f on the top half. I used the catalogue's naming: bank 't', rows a-e. Column strips behave the same either way.
The bent LED leg (column 6) is taken as the anode and the straight leg (column 8) as the cathode, as the schematic's current path requires.
A1 is read in the sketch but nothing is wired to it, so it has no edge. The LED is red in the image.
The parts are otherwise unchanged from step 1.
